name: Session in BSU
description: Polycarp studies in Berland State University. Soon he will have to take his exam. He has to pass exactly $$$n$$$ exams. For the each exam $$$i$$$ there are known two days: $$$a_i$$$ — day of the first opportunity to pass the exam, $$$b_i$$$ — day of the second opportunity to pass the exam ($$$a_i \lt b_i$$$). Polycarp can pass at most one exam during each day. For each exam Polycarp chooses by himself which day he will pass this exam. He has to pass all the $$$n$$$ exams. Polycarp wants to pass all the exams as soon as possible. Print the minimum index of day by which Polycarp can pass all the $$$n$$$ exams, or print -1 if he cannot pass all the exams at all.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^6$$$) — the number of exams. The next $$$n$$$ lines contain two integers each: $$$a_i$$$ and $$$b_i$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \lt b_i \le 10^9$$$), where $$$a_i$$$ is the number of day of the first passing the $$$i$$$-th exam and $$$b_i$$$ is the number of day of the second passing the $$$i$$$-th exam.
output_specification: If Polycarp cannot pass all the $$$n$$$ exams, print -1 . Otherwise print the minimum index of day by which Polycarp can do that.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1027F — Session in BSU [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
